title: Twice the speed. How much farther to stop? Four times: 12.3 m from 50 km/h, 49.2 m from 100 km/h
description:
Twice the speed. How much farther to stop? Two cars in the two lanes of one road, front bumpers on the same line, both braking at a constant 0.8 g (7.85 m/s^2, a dry-road figure) with no reaction time: this is braking distance only, the reaction distance is excluded. The left car starts at 50 km/h, the right car at 100 km/h. Both are drawn from the closed forms x = v0 t - a t^2 / 2 and v = v0 - a t and checked by an RK4 integration at 6,000 steps per second. The stop marks of the first run stay on the road for the later runs, so you can watch the fast car pass the slow car's stop mark. Played at 1/3 speed; deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- from 50 km/h (13.89 m/s): stops in 12.294 m after 1.770 s
- from 100 km/h (27.78 m/s): stops in 49.176 m after 3.541 s; four times the distance (ratio 4.0000) and twice the time for twice the speed
- where the 50 km/h car stops (12.29 m), the 100 km/h car is still doing 24.06 m/s = 86.6 km/h, 0.474 s after the line, with 75 percent of its kinetic energy left
- at the instant the 50 km/h car stops (1.770 s), the 100 km/h car is at 36.88 m doing exactly 50 km/h, with exactly 12.29 m still to go
- other speeds at 0.8 g, braking distance only: 30 km/h 4.43 m in 1.06 s; 70 km/h 24.10 m in 2.48 s; 130 km/h 83.11 m in 4.60 s
- RK4 checks: positions match the closed forms to 1.0e-11 m and speeds to 9.2e-12 m/s; interpolated stops 12.2940 m and 49.1761 m; speed at the slow car's mark 86.60 km/h

Why: the same brakes take away the same speed every second, so the fast car, with twice the speed to shed, brakes for twice as long. And it is faster the whole way: its average speed over the stop is twice the slow car's. Twice the time at twice the average speed is four times the distance. Stopping distance grows with the square of the speed, so 100 km/h against 70 km/h, 43 percent more speed, needs twice the road (49.2 m against 24.1 m). Reaction distance, which grows only in proportion to the speed, comes on top of this.

Rerun sims/braking/braking.py with projects/braking/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
